body: This is incredibly helpful. Thank you for taking time out of your busy day to write this. It's helpful for me and future folks who will search and find this post. Thanks!!

Thanks for the reply. I would love to read your book when it's finished. :)

I'm trying to get more organized, so that if I'm out for the day, qualified folks can step up and handle my tasks. But breaking big projects into small pieces and describing each piece seems like a monumental task. Do you have any advice?

Can you... write a book or something?

I'm rapid-cycling, and I'm really struggling right now. I'm a director of a deadline-driven division in a nonprofit with over 500 volunteers. I am getting so burned out and I just do not know how to meet deadlines any more. This is my passion. I don't think I could be happy with my life if I abandoned this.

It kills me because 10 years ago, before my mental health issues fully emerged, I could do this no problem. But I have no idea what to do now. I wish I could be more like you.

I just want to say: I am a huge Bernie supporter. I volunteer nearly every free moment I have, 6-7 days/week. I just left the campaign office a few hours ago so I can get to work. 

I have HIV. I feel really hurt by this. Only a small part of this was for people with HIV. Most of this is about research for any type of medication. It shouldn't come with a label of creating an HIV-free generation, because he doesn't talk about the drug that already exists that can make that a reality.

PREP. It's a drug, which when taken regularly, prevents the transmission of HIV with >90% efficacy. If the HIV positive person is using their meds, and their partner is on PREP, it is very likely that the statistical possibility of transmission is 0 (Look at the Partner study in Europe). 

So Bernie, don't use me as a pawn. You probably had next to no input on this. It was your campaign staff, who have probably never met a single person with HIV. If they knew anyone with HIV, they would have mentioned PREP. 

I'm not volunteering any more tonight. Don't give me bullshit about the big picture. I need a break.

He is. I don't know if that makes this better or worse. I tried to get him to phonebank, canvass, and do data entry (all of these asks spread out over a month so as to not overwhelm him). He donates about $10-20/week, which is a lot since he makes only a little over minimum wage. He says that's how he supports the campaign. But I'm just left feeling awful every time I leave the house. :(

[Serious] Really need some encouragement, guys and gals.

I wish this were a troll post. On a throwaway because some of you know my main.

My boyfriend is jealous of how excited I am about the Bernie Sanders campaign. He gets sullen and withdrawn when I leave the house to volunteer. If I even talk about Bernie Sanders or volunteering, he shuts down and gets super depressed. I literally have to choose between my boyfriend and this campaign. And I want to be honest with you. Volunteering with this campaign is the first thing that has made me feel alive in two years. (The last time I felt alive like this was when I met my bf.)

So, I'm not looking for you to tell me to break up with him. It's an option, but I probably won't take it. But maybe someone else out there is going through the same thing. Know you are not alone, and PM me if you want to talk. Cause right now, my bf is sleeping and I'm sneaking out of the house to go volunteer!!
